domains.name: Professional Conduct, Safety, and Risk Management

domain_guidance.summary: Domain 1 covers the client interview and assessment process used to gather medical history, risk factors, and baseline function before exercise programming. It establishes the information needed to screen and evaluate each client.

study_focus: Frequency, intensity, time, and type parameters
domain_guidance.summary: Domain 2 addresses program design and implementation, translating assessment findings into individualized exercise prescriptions. It covers selecting appropriate exercises, determining intensities, frequencies, times, and types, and structuring sessions for clients with medical conditions, while also emphasizing monitoring outcomes and documentation of progress.

Domain 3 focuses on progressing and modifying exercise programs as clients adapt or as their medical status changes. It covers adjusting loads, volumes, and exercises to maintain safety and continued benefit.

Domain 4 covers professional conduct, safety, and risk management in medical exercise practice. It addresses scope of practice, emergency response planning, documentation standards, ethical decision‑making, and legal considerations such as liability and client confidentiality.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early with valid ID and your ACE-CPT or equivalent prerequisite documentation. Pace yourself across the 150 questions in 165 minutes, and read each multiple-choice option carefully before selecting.

faq.answer_text: The ACE-MES exam contains 150 multiple-choice questions delivered in a linear format. Candidates answer all items in a single sitting without skipping or returning to previous questions.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the ACE-MES exam is 500. Scores are reported on a scaled scale, so the number reflects performance relative to the passing standard rather than a percentage of correct answers.

Candidates have 165 minutes to complete the ACE-MES exam, which consists of 150 multiple-choice questions presented in a linear format. The allotted time allows you to work through each item sequentially without the ability to return to previous questions.
The exam-only fee is $349, and a bundle with study materials is priced at $499. Candidates must hold an active ACE-CPT or equivalent credential before registering.
faq.question_title: How much does the ACE-MES exam cost?

faq.answer_text: The ACE-MES certification remains active for two years from the date of issuance. To maintain credential status, you must complete the required renewal process before expiration, which typically involves continuing education credits and adherence to ACE Fitness renewal policies.
faq.question_title: How long is the certification valid?

faq.answer_text: Yes, the ACE-MES is a current ACE Fitness certification and the exam content reflects the latest industry standards for medical exercise. For any future updates or changes to the certification pathway, always check directly with ACE Fitness for the most accurate information.
faq.question_title: Is the ACE-MES exam still current?

editorial.meta_description: ACE Medical Exercise Specialist (ACE-MES) exam covers client assessments, program design, progression, and safety for medical exercise practice.

methodology.summary: This page was built from ACE Fitness study documentation and the ACE Fitness exam guide, cross-referenced with public guidance on physical activity and clinical exercise prescription.

editorial.overview: The ACE Medical Exercise Specialist (ACE-MES) exam is administered by ACE Fitness and certifies professionals to design and deliver safe exercise programs for clients with medical conditions. It is a linear, multiple‑choice assessment built around four practice domains, and it evaluates knowledge of client interviews, program design, progression strategies, and professional conduct. The test consists of 150 multiple‑choice items presented in a linear format, and candidates have 165 minutes to complete it, requiring mastery of assessment, design, progression, and risk‑management principles.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Build a detailed study plan that maps each of the four domains to case examples from your client base, allocating focused time for review, practice questions, and skill reinforcement. Use the ACE Fitness study documentation together with the official exam guide, supplement with timed practice exams, and rehearse multiple‑choice questions under exam‑like conditions to become comfortable with the 150‑question, 165‑minute format.
skills_summary: Applying professional conduct and risk management
editorial.who_should_take: The ACE-MES is intended for fitness professionals who already hold an active ACE-CPT or equivalent credential and want to work with medically complex clients. It suits trainers moving into clinical or post-rehabilitation exercise settings.

exam_price_notes: Exam-only fee $349. With study materials bundle $499. Prerequisite: active ACE-CPT or equivalent.
exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials permitted. No personal items allowed in testing area. CPR/AED certification required for all ACE credentials.
id_requirements: One valid government-issued photo ID. Name must match ACE registration exactly.

lifecycle.summary: Confirmed current on the issuer host on 2026-09-19: "The ACE Medical Exercise Specialist Study Program prepares exercise professionals to collaborate with the healthcare community to help individuals coping with one or more diseases or disorders, or following rehabilitation to reach their health and fitness goals."

renewal_options: Certifications valid for 2 years. Renewal requires 20 CE credits and an active CPR/AED certification. Credits earned through ACE-approved continuing education courses, workshops, and professional development activities.

retake_policy.notes: 30-day waiting period between exam attempts. Full exam fee required for each retake attempt.
